clue.text: What fell off the head and right into the pudding

indicators.note: into says the and-plus-right pair goes inside the pudding word

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something tumbled off someone's head straight into the dessert bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFF is a traditional British steamed pudding (plum duff).
explanation.definitionFit: Dandruff is the flaky scurf that falls from the scalp.

clue.text: To change one's allegiance is something wrong

definitions.meaning: to desert one side for another

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means desert to the other side; as a noun, a flaw or imperfection.

clue.text: Admiral discovered in the hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio, the naval commander killed at Trafalgar
a wrestling grip applied from behind the neck

explanation.definitionFit: The famous naval commander of Trafalgar shares his surname with a wrestling grip.

clue.text: Soldier on errand of forgiveness- 11658 19

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, standing for a soldier
a mission is a task one is sent on

explanation.surface: A soldier sent on a task of pardoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission of sins is their pardon by God.

clue.text: If reception's faulty, get this picture in the first place

indicators.note: faulty means broken or garbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its s kept, giving all its letters

explanation.surface: Bad television reception means you see this image first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' jumbles IF RECEPTIONS, the s of 'reception's' counted as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The illustration facing the title page, at the very front of a book.

clue.text: Old county is giving Macbeth a title

parts.note: Glam. is the abbreviation for Glamorgan, a former Welsh county
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historic county is said to bestow a noble rank on Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan was a Welsh county abolished in 1974; 'Old county' suggests the definition, but it gives only the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is hailed by the witches as Thane of Glamis, his first rank in the play.

clue.text: Tours in this valley

parts.note: Tours is a French city, not a holiday trip, lying in a river valley famed for its châteaux

explanation.surface: Sightseeing trips in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city of Tours stands on the river whose valley is famed for châteaux.

clue.text: Leonid's career could be so described

definitions.text: Leonid's career could be so described

parts.words: Leonid's career could be so described
parts.note: Leonid looks like a man's name, but the Leonids are a November shower of shooting stars streaking across the sky

explanation.surface: A Russian man named Leonid had a rapid rise to fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift, brilliant career is likened to a shooting star, and a Leonid literally is one.

clue.text: Suitable material on a worker, painter or conductor, say?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the material sits above the worker

parts.note: serge is cloth for making suits
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Asks which cloth would suit a labourer, an artist or a bandleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a sound-alike: the military rank sounds like Sargent, the painter John Singer Sargent or the conductor Sir Malcolm Sargent.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank's spoken form matches the surname of the portraitist and the British orchestral leader.

clue.text: When Cynthia looks round

parts.note: Cynthia is a poetic name for the moon goddess, so this is the time her face appears as a complete disc

explanation.surface: Asks when a woman named Cynthia turns her head.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the whole disc is lit makes the goddess's face look circular.

clue.text: It can carry one horizontally? rubbish!-

definitions.meaning: a stretcher or couch on poles bearing a person lying down

explanation.definitionFit: A curtained couch borne on poles carries a reclining person, and strewn waste is also called by this word.

clue.text: Causing grief and terror, a riot'in the cooler

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Grief and terror caused by a riot in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cooler' is slang for prison, but here 'cooler' is the definition. 'riot' scrambles GRIEF, TERROR and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance that keeps food chilled.

clue.text: Thwart appears to go from side to side

definitions.meaning: to traverse, pass over from one side to the other

explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan and to pass over a road are both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: Hence the arbiter of sport or entertainment initially

parts.note: taken as written
a referee, ref for short, judges a match
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of entertainment

explanation.surface: Seems to describe who adjudicates either a game or a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean for that reason, as a consequence.

clue.text: Lamb's thesis upon Roast Pig involved Edison with artist

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb's essay on roast pork somehow drew in the inventor Edison and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the essay 'A Dissertation upon Roast Pig'. 'involved' scrambles EDISON with ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb's essay title calls it a learned discourse, a formal treatise on a subject.

clue.text: A farm yield's including oil possibly — a high spot in the City

indicators.note: including means the word for harvests holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: crops are what a farm yields, with the s from the possessive

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of oil may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A harvest that contains oil, maybe, is the peak of the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns OIL into OLI, which goes into CROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortified hilltop citadel of an ancient Greek city, notably Athens.

clue.text: Relating to cultivation damaged by Niagara River

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Farmland harmed by the Niagara River flooding.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned with the land and farming.

clue.text: Youngster takes place of driver on horse, with hesitation

parts.note: in golf, the driver club is used from the tee
a nag is an old horse
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A youth takes the coachman's seat, hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist or coachman; it is a golf club, played from the TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person.

clue.text: Successful gardeners keep them at arm's length

definitions.text: Successful gardeners keep them at arm's length

parts.words: Successful gardeners keep them at arm's length
parts.note: skilled growers are said to have a natural knack in their hands, and the digits sit at the far end of each arm

explanation.surface: Good gardeners hold something away from themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a talent with plants refers to verdant digits, which literally lie at the end of the arm.

clue.text: Though senile he has a way to support Dorothy

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit beneath the name

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: An old man, though doddering, has a way to help Dorothy.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddering old man weakened by age.

clue.text: But might I of Jove's — sup" (Jonson)

definitions.text: But might I of Jove's — sup" (Jonson)

parts.words: But might I of Jove's — sup" (Jonson)
parts.note: the missing word from Ben Jonson's song 'To Celia' (Drink to me only with thine eyes)

explanation.surface: A line of Jonson's verse with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonson's lover would not swap her kiss even for the drink of the gods.

clue.text: No heavyweight, said King the newscaster

indicators.note: said means the phrase for a light weight is spoken to give a verb of declaring

parts.note: an ounce is a tiny weight, nothing heavy
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reported to be no heavyweight, according to someone called King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns AN OUNCE into its spoken twin ANNOUNCE; R (Rex) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reads out the news on radio or television.

clue.text: Join regiment, say, before end of June

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: a regiment is an example of a military unit

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of June

explanation.surface: Enlist in the army ahead of the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine or bring together.

clue.text: Spacecraft for finding beryllium

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Be is the chemical symbol for beryllium

explanation.surface: A space vehicle designed to locate a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmanned vehicle sent to explore space is called this.

clue.text: She's riding the first half last

indicators.note: the opening half of the word riding is moved to its end

explanation.surface: A woman on horseback came first, then half came last.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'She's' as 'She is': the answer is a woman's name. RID-ING becomes ING-RID.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, as of the actress Bergman, fits a clue asking who a woman is.

clue.text: Strong supporter of law reform in the beginning

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the word for beginning

parts.note: start means the beginning

indicators.note: reform means to reshape, so the letters of law are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm backer of changing the legal system from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns LAW into ALW, which 'in' places inside START.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal, dependable backer of a cause or party.

clue.text: Tended to reverse sequence, but in Latin form

indicators.note: reverse means the word for a sequence is written backwards

parts.note: a run is an unbroken series
sed is the Latin word for but

explanation.surface: Someone tended to change the order of things, but in a classical way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns RUN into NUR. 'Tended to' looks like 'was inclined to'; here it means looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: Cared for a patient or looked after something carefully.

clue.text: Coeur de Lion for instance was less refined about it

indicators.note: about means the word for less refined goes around the other piece

parts.note: cruder means rougher, less polished
it is slang for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: Richard the Lionheart was apparently somewhat coarse in his manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I, nicknamed the Lionheart, led the Third Crusade, so he is an example of a holy warrior.
